sections.brief: How Israel obtained a plutonium-production complex from France, 1955–1960, in order: Atoms for Peace (12 July 1955) and the small US-built Soreq reactor (contract 20 March 1957, critical June 1960); Bergmann's failed 1956 approach to the AEC; Peres's September 1956 request in Paris for a reactor and a reprocessing plant (Goldschmidt's recollection, labelled as such, with Perrin's hesitation); the 1957 agreements (18 MW offered in 1956, 24 MW signed, systems built for three times that, reprocessing in unwritten protocols; The National Interest's three-contract version with 385 tonnes of uranium, attributed). Present the signing-date dispute in full (3 or 30 October; 1 October backdated to 30 September; Peres's own memoir). Then secret construction under Manes Pratt (about 1,500 workers, the desalination cover at French customs), Norway's 20 tons of heavy water (25 February 1959) against FAS's four tons flown by the French air force, de Gaulle's May 1960 demand and Aronson's 'abrogate' account, and the 1960 compromise, with JVL's 'little changed' and the November 1960 dating; close on the Leibowitz–Livne committee as the only public dissent. Keep the US discovery for cw4_dimona_discovery and the Kennedy letters for cw5 ([scene:s11b|the 1963 letters]). Figures: timeline 1955–1960; comparison of what France agreed in 1956, 1957 and the 1960 compromise.

The periphery doctrine from its roots in 1957 to the Trident of autumn 1958: Ben-Gurion's 1957 view of Turkey (letter of 15 September, diary of 16 October), Haile Selassie's approach of February 1957, Sasson's meeting with Menderes in Paris (15 December 1957) and Menderes's Syria proposal that Ben-Gurion rejected, the government decision of 20 July 1958 (with Schonmann's Israel State Archives citations), the 24 July letter to Eisenhower (give both renderings of the 'dam' sentence), the secret August 1958 agreement with Menderes (present the Ankara-visit and embassy-level dispute from both sides), and the Trident's first meetings (late September–October 1958). From ira_s00c tell only the 1958 formation and the lopsided structure (Alpher's account, labelled as a participant's); the 1973 embargo and 1975 interview link forward. From tk_s03 tell only the 1958 pact; 1949 is Volume II's and 1996 is later. Present Washington's reception from both sides (Alpher's 'lukewarm blessing' against the Policy Planning Staff's 'not firm' and Dulles's 'extreme caution'). Name the term 'periphery' as Israel's own policy language and examine it; do not present the partners' peoples as instruments. Map: turkey_arc. Figure: timeline February 1957–October 1958.

The year the region turned, February–October 1958: the United Arab Republic and the rival Arab Union; Lebanon's crisis from May (Chamoun's second-term bid, SNIE 36.4–58's own words, Chamoun's charge against Nasser and the UN inspectors' finding, UNOGIL's nearly 600 observers and 49 posts); the Baghdad coup of 14 July and the deaths of Faisal II, the crown prince and Nuri al-Sa'id; Eisenhower's NSC meeting and memoir line; Operation Blue Bat (1,700 first ashore; the peak given as almost 15,000 or about 14,000; one combat death; about $200 million; out by 25 October) and the British contingent to Amman; Chehab's election. Present Lebanese domestic causes and the Nasserist-subversion reading side by side, and Kennedy's and Fulbright's opposition. End with Israel's position as its envoys gave it to Dulles in London on 27 July and Eisenhower's 25 July letter. From me_s08 tell only the UAR and Iraq 1958 (earlier coups are Volume II's and cw1–cw3's). Map: me_layers.

The August 1958 overflight crisis day by day (1–10 August): the British paratroop flights and the US airlift over Israel, the Soviet note of 1 August and Dulles's letter of the same date, Comay's stop order of 2 August and Lawson's reading of cabinet pressure, Dulles's rebuke to Eban and Herzog on 3 August, the 5 August meeting with Herter and Peres (Ben-Gurion's letter on arms and the unwritten guarantee), the resumption on 6 and 10 August. Present the dispute over Ben-Gurion's motive from both sides (the Soviet note vs domestic and British politics as Eban and JTA's Israeli sources gave it) and Schonmann's 'accidental crisis' thesis as her interpretation. Figure: timeline 1–10 August 1958; comparison of what Israel asked (arms, a written guarantee, support for the periphery) and what Dulles offered.

Wadi Salib, Haifa, July–August 1959, in order: the neighbourhood's Palestinian past and its emptying in 1948, then its North African Jewish residents; the shooting of Akiva Yaakov Elkrif on the night of 8 July (give the dispute over the arrest); Ben-Harush's procession of 9 July and the broadsheet 'Is Our Blood Cheap?'; the clashes (13 police and 2 demonstrators hurt, 34 arrested) and the spread to Beersheba, Acre, Tiberias and Migdal HaEmek; the Etzioni commission (19 July–17 August; 46 witnesses; 'half of [the protestors] were children, women, and adolescents'); its reported finding of no deliberate institutional discrimination, given as reported and set against the protesters' account and the scholarship (Naor; Romanenko); Khoushi's and Mapai's responses; Ben-Harush's list in the 1959 election; the Youth Law and Child Benefit Law that followed. Never generalize about a community: name the union, the officials and the documents. Link back to [scene:rd6_ingathering|the mass immigration]. Figure: timeline 8 July–17 August 1959; comparison of the protesters' and the state's accounts. Still open: the commission report's exact wording on discrimination (only a secondary summary was fetched) and Ben-Harush's vote count and sentence.

Palestinian politics 1957–1962 on both sides of the line. Fatah: the Kuwait core group (autumn 1957 per the Institute for Palestine Studies; 1959 per some founders; present both), Filastinuna (Beirut, October 1959), the reversed slogan 'the liberation of Palestine is the road to Arab unity', independence from Arab regimes, and a forward link to the PLO (1964, cw6). From hma_src_s02 tell only Fatah's founding. Inside Israel: Al-Ard from 1959, its one-issue-a-year newspaper tactic, the convictions, the printing company registered in early 1962 after the Supreme Court ruling, its bylaws' two-states sentence and Ben-Gurion's 'two organizations which resent Israel'; tell the 1964 ban and the 1965 disqualification in one forward paragraph. Present both readings of Al-Ard (rights movement vs threat) with the court's majority and dissent. Military government continues: link [scene:mg_s01|military rule]. Still open: the Arab Nationalist Movement in 1957–62 and the date of the Supreme Court ruling on the company.

The armistice lines 1960–1962 from UN and US records: the demilitarized-zone cultivation dispute at Beit Katzir and the Chief of Staff's proposal of 20 January 1960; Tawafiq (31 January–1 February 1960) with the MAC's condemnation and Israel's case side by side, and the casualty figures attributed to their source; Radio Cairo of 3 February; the Rotem crisis (Egyptian divisions into Sinai, Israel surprised, 7,000 reservists, withdrawal from 9 March), attributed to the scholarship it rests on and labelled a 'trial run' for 1967 as an interpretation; then the Lake Tiberias exchanges from 8 March 1962, the raid of 16–17 March, Israel's counter-claims and sovereignty claim, resolution 171 (9 April 1962) and the US account of how its draft lost 'balance'. Both sides' cases at full strength. The water war of 1964–67 is cw6's ([scene:sy_s02|the DMZs and the water war]). Figure: timeline January 1960–April 1962. Still open: the Rotem crisis from a primary or non-Wikipedia secondary text beyond Bar-Joseph's title, and casualties of March 1962.

Israel's European support, 1957–1962, centred on West Germany: Peres and Strauss in Bonn (3 July 1957; submarines bought in Britain with German money; about $30 million of Israeli materiel bought by Germany), Harman's request of 1 February 1960 and Ben-Gurion's 10 March appointment with Eisenhower, the Waldorf meeting of 14 March 1960 (no transcript; 'the Germany of today is not the Germany of yesterday'; the $500 million request), and 'Aktion Geschäftsfreund' with its yearly mark figures (82, 97.6, 150, 149.8, 150 million; 629.4 million to 1965) and the 340 vs 500 million mark arms figures. Present the Dimona-funding dispute at full strength on both sides (Bar-Joseph and Die Welt vs the missing records, the absent transcript and Peres's denial), and the two Peres versions of who paid ($40 million from donors vs from the government). Name Globke and Oberländer as documented, and the 1964–65 end of secrecy and the 12 May 1965 relations as a forward link. From arm_s07 and s19g tell only the founding of Labour Friends of Israel in 1957 and the point that Germany's support rests on state policy rather than an organized lobby; the 2006–2025 material links forward. Link back to [scene:rd6_financing|reparations] in one sentence. Figure: money chain for Aktion Geschäftsfreund (Bonn budget, Frankfurt development bank booked as developing-country transfers, interest at 3.6%, Israel's Negev account, the unresolved end use).

Eichmann from capture to execution, as politics: the seizure in Buenos Aires (11 May 1960) and the flight of 20 May; Ben-Gurion's authorization of Harel; the cabinet and Knesset of 23 May; Israel's 'volunteers' note and Meir's 'not a normal case'; Argentina's recall of its ambassador and complaint; resolution 138 (23 June 1960) in its own words and vote; Amadeo's ambiguity; the joint statement of 3 August 1960. Then the trial's politics from the Israel State Archives: Bureau 06, Ben-Gurion's principles of 29 May 1960, the West German and Globke dimension (with cw4_europe's Strauss material), the 6–5 vote on defence witnesses, the clemency decision, Buber and Bergman's appeal, and the effect on Israeli memory and on Nazi prosecutions worldwide. Present both disputes (state operation vs 'volunteers'; whether the Council condemned Israel). Do not retell the trial's documents: link [scene:rd4_documents|the documents of the Holocaust] (court case 40/61, 1,600 documents, 108 witnesses are told there). Figure: timeline May 1960–June 1962. Still open: the Argentine expulsion of Israel's ambassador (only the recall of Argentina's own ambassador was verified) and Arendt's and her critics' arguments.

Iran and Israel, 1957–1960: the oil trade from late 1956 and the Eilat pipeline's dependence on Iranian crude (the Rothschild-group contract), SAVAK's approach in 1957 and Harel's visit of February 1958 (Schonmann), the 1958 Ahvaz broadcasting station (reported), Bakhtiar's secret talk with Ben-Gurion and his complaint that Iran felt 'let down', Israeli agricultural experts in Iran, and the July 1960 recognition crisis: the Shah's statement, Nasser's speech, Aram's reply, al-Azhar's telegram and the break. Present both disputes (1949 vs 1950 for de facto recognition; Israel vs the Gulf as the cause of the break). Note the open question of which year the FRUS telegram belongs to (its file number reads August 1959 while its note describes the Shah's July 1960 statement). Link back to cw1 for 1947–53 and to [scene:ira_s00b|the 1954 consortium] for SAVAK's founding.

How Washington found Dimona, April 1958–1 December 1960, as an intelligence story: the 1958 embassy queries and Bergmann's denial, the post-mortem's finding that information from April 1958 and mid-1959 was discounted, the U-2 dispute (present all three positions), the AMF employee's '60 megawatt' report and Despatch 75 (2 August 1960), the 'textile plant' (with its date problem), the French denial of 22 November, Herter to Caccia, and Gomberg's 'weapons grade plutonium' debriefing. End with the 2 December JAEIC report and the 8 December estimate, and Burr and Cohen's 'intelligence failure' and 'counterintelligence success' judgments, labelled as theirs. Figure: timeline April 1958–8 December 1960; process flow of how a report moved (embassy, State, CIA/JAEIC, NSC).

The disclosure month, 7 December 1960–19 January 1961: the summons of the Israeli ambassador, Couve de Murville's 'replica of Marcoule' and 'assumed the money came from US', McCone on Meet the Press, Eisenhower's 19 December meeting (his words on funds and US aid; Gates; McCone's separation plant), Harman's '24 megawatts' account, Ben-Gurion's Knesset statement (both quotations and the 21 vs 22 December dispute), Addy Cohen's 'misbehaving', 'Why in the States is everything being told to everybody?', the 'lack of candor' and 'by no means come clean' cables, the embassy's cost estimate set against Herter's $40–80 million and Eisenhower's $100–200 million, Ben-Gurion's 4 January refusal of IAEA inspection, and the plutonium-to-France assurance. From cia_s16 tell only its 1960 starting point (French assistance and the policy of ambiguity) and from cia_s07 only that its pattern is dated from the 1960s; NUMEC is cw6's ([scene:fis_s07a|NUMEC]), and cia_s16's statement that the arsenal was built partly with uranium stolen from NUMEC must be presented as contested, not as fact. Vanunu, Symington and the warhead estimates link forward. Figure: comparison of what Israel said in December 1960 and what US officials concluded; key figures of the cost estimates.

The Lavon affair reopened, autumn 1960–August 1961: Lavon's charge of forgery and perjury, the Cohn finding and Hausner's opinion (the 6–5 cabinet vote), Peres's testimony, Ben-Gurion's demand for a judicial commission; the Committee of Seven under Rosen (report of 25 December 1960) and Gibli's departure; Ben-Gurion's 'half-truths' and his brief retreat; the Histadrut resignations and Lavon's refusal; Ben-Gurion's resignation of 31 January 1961; Lavon's removal by the party's central committee; the election of 15 August 1961 (seat figures) and the four-month coalition talks. From lv_s01 tell only 1960–61 (Stage Two tells 1954–55); correct its 1963 line by giving both resignations with dates. Present the Britannica date conflict. Figure: timeline October 1960–August 1961; key figures for the 1961 election. Still open: the exact date and vote of Lavon's removal from the Histadrut (February 1961 is not yet verified) and the Elad trial's role.

Kennedy's first months on Dimona, 20 January–26 May 1961: Rusk's memorandum of 30 January ('categoric assurances', 'a continuing subject'), Reid's 'on a secret basis', the waiting from January to the April invitation and Israel's request for secrecy, Harman's linkage of the visit to a meeting with Kennedy, Gazit's hint, Meir's reported objection, and the Staebler–Croach visit (give the 18/20/17–22 May dating dispute) with their findings in their own words. Then present the dispute at full strength: the scientists' 'nothing was concealed' and 'no present evidence' against Cohen and Burr's case that the visits were staged and the separation plant hidden. Stop before the 1963 letters ([scene:s11b|Kennedy and Dimona, 1963]). Figure: timeline January–May 1961.

The Kennedy–Ben-Gurion meeting at the Waldorf-Astoria, 30 May 1961, from the record: who was there, the Dimona exchange ('plutonium producing capability'; 'for the time being, only'; a plutonium plant in three or four years; the Scandinavians and the Swiss), the weapons and Hawk exchange, and the refugee exchange (Ben-Gurion's 'best weapon at hand' and Kennedy's 70% of UNRWA's costs), set against the unedited draft and the Israeli minutes ('we will see what happens in the Middle East'). Then the State Department's briefing of ten Arab states' representatives and Ben-Gurion's 'It's worth a try' on the Conciliation Commission, and the second, unannounced 40-minute visit of 26 September 1962 with the October 1962 assurance to Nasser. Give the visit-count dispute (seven or eight in the 1960s) and link forward to [scene:s11b|1963]. Figure: comparison of the official memorandum, the draft and the Israeli minutes on Dimona's purpose.

The Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (Public Law 87–195) and AID (Executive Order 10973, 3 November 1961) as the legal frame of US aid; FY1962 appropriations ($4.515 billion); the CRS series of US aid to Israel 1956–1963 with the small military loans of 1959–60 and $13.2 million in 1962. From law_s01 tell only the statute: Section 620I carries the 1961 Act's numbering but was enacted on 30 September 1996 (Public Law 104–208), born of Turkey's blockade of Armenia; correct law_s01's 1961 dating explicitly and link its 2024 application forward. Dashboard: aid_arms:Overview:2 may be shared with cw4_hawk; discuss its rows here only if cw4_hawk does not. Figure: key figures of aid to Israel 1957–1962. Still open: the date Kennedy signed the Act (not found in the fetched pages).

Morocco's Jews 1956–1962: the emigration ban (1956 or 1959; present both), clandestine departure of about 30,000, the Egoz (10 January 1961; 44 or 46 dead, give both), Hassan II's accession (26 February 1961), the negotiations (Gatmon, Moulay Ali, Benjelloun, HIAS) and the payments ($500,000; $100; $250), and the start of Operation Yachin (end of November 1961), with its 1961–64 total stated as a forward-reaching range (90,000–97,000). Give the Moroccan government's motives, Moroccan Jewish critics (Levy, Miller) and the rescue reading side by side; never generalize about Moroccans or Jews. From oa_s03 tell only 1961–62; earlier years are [scene:oa_s03|Volume II's account]. Still open: a primary or scholarly text for the agreement's terms (the payment figures rest on secondary and advocacy sources and Wikipedia's citations of Laskier, Bialer and Szulc).

The Hawk decision from refusal to offer, 1960–August 1962: the 1960 refusals ($40 million for six batteries), the 1961 cost estimate and the $1 million ceiling of earlier sales, Kennedy's May 1961 'a defensive weapon ... also a missile', the June 1962 deferral paper, Rusk's review of 7 August, Feldman's memorandum of 10 August tying the Hawk to the Johnson refugee plan (with its figures), the 19 August meeting with Ben-Gurion, Meir and Kollek, Rusk's 21 August 'statement in principle', approval on credit, the 7 September 'purely defensive' instruction, and first deliveries in 1965. Present the three disputes (was Nasser told; balance and refugees vs domestic politics; whether military aid began in 1959 or 1962) and correct s11d's 'offensive' wording. Dashboard: aid_arms:Overview:2, discussing its '1948–1961 economic aid only' and '1962 first US military aid — as loans' rows against the CRS figures. Link the December 1962 'special relationship' talk forward to cw5. Figure: timeline 1960–September 1962. Still open: the sale's final price and credit terms, and documented Arab and Soviet reactions.
